newsitem.title: USA: DELL CEO says PC sales via Internet booming.
newsitem.headline: DELL CEO says PC sales via Internet booming.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp. Chairman Michael Dell said the company's sales of personal computers over the Internet are booming and are now approaching an annual value of $500 million.
He said in a keynote address at the PC Expo trade show here that Dell's daily Internet sales are doubling to about $2 million a day from $1 million a day in the first quarter.
"So get out your credit cards and go to www.dell.com," he joked. "Dell.com brings us closer to our customers."
Dell, which sells PCs directly to its customers, said that the Internet is "turbocharging" Dell's direct sales model.

Customers configure their own PCs at Dell's Web site. Dell also said more than 5,000 Dell customers now have developed personalized Web pages that provide faster access to information and enable customers to configure products online and monitor the status of their orders.
Dell said the company's component suppliers will begin to benefit with a window onto Dell's factory show floors via the World Wide Web and links to Dell with Internet technology.
Dell also made some jabs at the NC, the network computer concept developed by Oracle Corp. and implemented by Sun Microsystems Inc., International Business Machines Corp. and others.
"The proposed NC is a proprietary solution," Dell said, adding that he agrees with Microsoft Corp. Chief Executive Bill Gates's description of the NC as being "not compatible."
The NC was developed as a device to access corporate networks and the Internet, running slimmed-down software applications.

Dell and 11 other PC makers Monday introduced the Net PC, the PC industry's answer to the NC, which is also aimed at lowering the increasing cost of computing. Dell said the Net PC will be used by a "narrow market" and that more users want so-called "managed PCs," which are more flexible.
Kevin Rollins, president of Dell Americas, said in an interview that he believes the Net PCs will be used by about 10 percent to 20 percent of corporate users.

"Our customers want this notion of a managed PC," Rollins said. Managed PCs are not stripped-down PCs, but are mostly controlled by the network manager, for things such as software upgrades and virus testing.

The Net PCS are stripped-down, diskless PCs that are connected and managed by a corporate network and are sealed. Rollins said taking away the floppy drive and CD-ROM player doesn't take too much off the cost.

"You will see Net PCs, sealed with no expansion capabilities, and those will be for very task-focused activities," Rollins said. Dell will have both Net PCs and managed PCs later this year, with pricing to be announced.
